\section[nakhaḥ]{\sk{नखः} (nakhaḥ) — a nail}

\label{lesson:SA-C70-nail}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for the forehead, then the Sanskrit for the tongue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{नखः}}
\textbf{\sk{नखः}} (\emph{nakhaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a nail\textquotedblright{}, at the tip of every finger.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The end of a finger.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nakhaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nakhaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nakhaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for the forehead, then the Sanskrit for the tongue, then say \emph{nakhaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{नखः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A nail\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[jānu]{\sk{जानु} (jānu) — the knee}

\label{lesson:SA-C70-knee}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for the tongue, then the Sanskrit for a fingernail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{जानु}}
\textbf{\sk{जानु}} (\emph{jānu}) — \textquotedblleft{}the knee\textquotedblright{}, halfway down the \textbf{\sk{पादः}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Where the leg bends.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jānu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{jānu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for the tongue, then the Sanskrit for a fingernail, then say \emph{jānu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{जानु} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The knee\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pṛṣṭham]{\sk{पृष्ठम्} (pṛṣṭham) — the back}

\label{lesson:SA-C70-back}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a fingernail, then the Sanskrit for the knee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पृष्ठम्}}
\textbf{\sk{पृष्ठम्}} (\emph{pṛṣṭham}) — \textquotedblleft{}the back\textquotedblright{}. The same word names the back of a page.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The side you cannot see.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pṛṣṭham}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pṛṣṭham}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{pṛṣṭham}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for a fingernail, then the Sanskrit for the knee, then say \emph{pṛṣṭham} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{पृष्ठम्} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The back\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[oṣṭhaḥ]{\sk{ओष्ठः} (oṣṭhaḥ) — the lip}

\label{lesson:SA-C70-lip}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for the back, then the Sanskrit for the shoulder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{ओष्ठः}}
\textbf{\sk{ओष्ठः}} (\emph{oṣṭhaḥ}) — \textquotedblleft{}the lip\textquotedblright{}. The sounds \textbf{\sk{प}} and \textbf{\sk{म}} are made with both lips.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The edge of the mouth.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṣṭhaḥ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṣṭhaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{oṣṭhaḥ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for the back, then the Sanskrit for the shoulder, then say \emph{oṣṭhaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{ओष्ठः} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The lip\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
